method: Read-only inspection of active Marketplace item pages, listing photos where available, and model-specific used-market/support evidence. `fit_rank` is category-specific for active audio interfaces; higher `score` is the dashboard's Best Fit sort value. Prices remain separate from third-party used-value evidence.

1793308288687102.condition: Exact generation appears in the listing title; functional condition and included cable/accessories remain to be verified at pickup.
1793308288687102.accessories: Not specified; verify USB cable and confirm all inputs, outputs, knob encoders, and headphone jack work.
1793308288687102.windows_status: Modern Focusrite USB interface with current Windows support; two mic preamps, four line inputs, balanced outputs, and MIDI make it a flexible recording foundation.
1793308288687102.research_notes: Best overall active interface value: $99 is below the reviewed $109–$165 used range and the 3rd Gen platform is a practical modern Windows choice. Test both preamps, all line I/O, headphones, USB connection, and MIDI before buying.

1624342312093126.condition: Seller describes it as used-like-new and barely used; photos show light surface dust/wear but no obvious impact damage.
1624342312093126.accessories: No USB cable, box, or power supply is shown or promised. It normally works over USB bus power; verify a USB-A-to-USB-B cable is included or budget for one.
1624342312093126.windows_status: Official Steinberg specifications include Windows 11 64-bit. Two D-PRE mic preamps, two combo inputs, direct monitoring, MIDI I/O, and 24-bit/192 kHz make it an excellent low-cost two-input foundation.
1624342312093126.research_notes: Exact model confirmed from the front-panel UR22mkII marking and rear USB 2.0/MIDI layout. At $30 it is below the current $38–$69 Reverb used estimate. Strong budget buy only after testing both inputs, headphone output, monitor outputs, MIDI, gain knobs, and USB connection.

2929178584094192.condition: Generation is stated in the listing title; test all front and rear I/O before purchase.
2929178584094192.accessories: Not specified; verify USB cable and power/connection setup as applicable.
2929178584094192.windows_status: Modern Focusrite USB platform with two mic preamps, expanded line I/O, balanced outputs, and MIDI; well suited to adding hardware instruments.
2929178584094192.research_notes: Good capability buy at $150, within the reviewed $117–$185 used range. Choose it over the 4i4 only if its expanded routing/line I/O will be useful soon.

1558017365599197.accessories: Shipped listing; confirm power/USB cable and return terms.
1558017365599197.windows_status: Two-input USB interface with balanced outputs and MIDI; a usable basic modern option.
1558017365599197.research_notes: Fair at $80, but not compelling beside the local $30 UR22mkII or $99 Scarlett 4i4. Prefer a local, testable modern interface.

2021195761823060.condition: Seller describes it as used-like-new, excellent working order, and minimally worn. The listing includes a short demo video and multiple photos.
2021195761823060.accessories: USB cable/box inclusion is not clearly promised in the description; confirm before buying.
2021195761823060.windows_status: Native Instruments lists PC compatibility through ASIO/DirectSound/WASAPI. It provides two mic/line/instrument inputs and balanced monitor outputs.
2021195761823060.research_notes: The $70 firm ask plus shipping is above the recent $55.99–$60 sale examples. Offer about $55–$60 delivered; otherwise the local Steinberg is better value.

1360246255985555.condition: Photos identify the original AudioBox USB from its front-panel marking. The underside shows routine cosmetic scuffs and worn rubber feet; functional condition remains to be verified at pickup.
1360246255985555.accessories: No USB cable, software, box, or other accessories are shown or promised.
1360246255985555.windows_status: Bus-powered 2-in/2-out USB audio and MIDI interface with two combo mic/instrument inputs, 48 kHz maximum sample rate, balanced outputs, and MIDI. PreSonus provides legacy drivers; confirm it connects and records reliably on the current Windows machine before buying.
1360246255985555.research_notes: The first photo establishes this as the original AudioBox USB, not the newer USB 96; the underside barcode U209091941 appears to be a serial/inventory identifier, not a model number. At $40 it is within the reviewed $29–$45 used range, so it is a fair local price rather than a standout deal. Prefer the $30 Steinberg UR22mkII for newer 192 kHz support and a better overall value, but this is a usable low-cost two-input/MIDI option if it passes a full test.
